A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BEAST research work. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic trajectory experiments, simulation benchmark evaluations, real-robot experiments, and ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds a shared-backbone tokenizer comparison and preliminary BEAST-Flow results in Section 5.4 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: Appendix D adds an evaluated BEAST-Flow variant combining continuous spline tokens with a flow-matching loss and a mixture-of-experts backbone; v1 described flow matching only as future work. The underlying tokenizer, boundary conditioning, and existing BEAST-F, BEAST-D, and BEAST-ACT procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic trajectory task, CALVIN, LIBERO, simulated ALOHA tasks, and eight real-world tasks. The added tokenizer and flow-matching experiments use the already-covered LIBERO-LONG and CALVIN ABC-to-D settings.

E2.justification: v3 adds FAST-AR to the Florence-2 tokenizer comparison, extending v1's same-backbone comparison against Binning-F. Appendix D also introduces an action-chunking Flow comparator for BEAST-Flow. The existing benchmark and real-robot comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: Section 5.4 introduces a substantial controlled comparison using Florence-2 without robot-data pretraining across tokenizers, including autoregressive and parallel BEAST decoding. Appendix D adds a flow-policy comparison with and without spline compression, and the basis-count sweep adds N=25. These are additional experimental designs; existing splits, training schedules, and robot evaluation procedures remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new shared-backbone study tests tokenizer differences while controlling architecture and robot pretraining, and directly compares autoregressive versus parallel BEAST decoding on two benchmarks. Table 4 also extends basis-count sensitivity to 25 bases and revises the 15- and 20-basis results. Existing continuous-token and model-size ablations are retained.

E5.justification: Existing uncertainty values and evaluation-run disclosures are retained. Neither the new tokenizer comparison nor the flow-matching results introduce seed counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 4 changes CALVIN average lengths for 15 bases from 4.14 to 4.20 and for 20 bases from 2.71 to 4.32, adding 4.23 for 25 bases. New Figure 8 reports FAST-AR versus BEAST-AR at 84% versus 84% on LIBERO-LONG and 46% versus 71% on CALVIN. Figure 11 adds Flow versus BEAST-Flow results of 91.5% versus 91.5% and 61.6% versus 63.6%, respectively. Main benchmark Tables 1–3 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The spline definitions, recurrence, regression formulation, and boundary-conditioning argument are retained. Changing the residual regression's optimization variable from c to c-hat is a notation correction, without a new derivation, assumption, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and central conclusion retain the same claims about training-free tokenization, fixed-length compression, smooth trajectories, architectural compatibility, and efficient competitive control. The conclusion's new pointer to preliminary flow-matching results adds support without redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B newly explains Florence-2's suitability through grounding-focused pretraining, low image-token count, and computational efficiency. Appendix A provides practical guidance addressing the retained basis-count sensitivity limitation. Existing interpretations concerning small real-world datasets and discrete representations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A documents basis selection using sampled trajectories, normalized reconstruction MSE below 0.01, and a search for the smallest adequate basis count. Appendix B adds Florence-2 implementation detail, including 50 image tokens, and the project-page link destination changes. Existing hyperparameter, robot-hardware, and compute-resource disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive connection to movement primitives, including DMPs, ProDMP, and prior B-spline movement primitives. It explicitly distinguishes their continuous representations and predominant reinforcement-learning applications from BEAST's positioning. This acknowledges a closely related methodological lineage absent from v1's discussion; additional references support flow matching and architecture details.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized clarifications, corrects the architecture count from two to three, expands architecture explanations, and inserts a comparison subsection and two appendices. Affiliations, publication footer, acknowledgments, and cross-references are updated. Most existing prose and the overall narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds the tokenizer-comparison and flow-matching bar charts as Figures 8 and 11, and adds a row to Table 4. Existing figures are retained with relocation or renumbering; Figure 6 has simplified labels and rounded annotations. The overall visual design and existing architecture diagrams remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The shared-Florence comparison reduces backbone and pretraining confounds in v1's FAST comparisons, while basis-selection guidance and movement-primitive positioning improve usability and context. These gains support a net improvement, but the new experiments lack uncertainty reporting and detailed protocols. Table 4's revisions are unexplained, and its added 25-basis setting for 20-step chunks is not reconciled with Section 4.1's N ≤ T restriction, limiting the overall gain.
